request.spec:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Patrons and backing are in, and all 4 tests in the acceptance spec pass under `bin/e2e`.

**How it behaves**
- Each person's row has a picker listing everyone on the sheet, and an "Add patron" button.
- If the person picks themselves or someone they already named, the server refuses it. The row shows an error (`person-patron-error`), and nothing is stored or audited. The error clears when the picker changes or the button is pressed again.
- An accepted patron is stored and writes `PATRON_ADDED sheet=<id> by=<user> name=<name> patron=<patron name>` to the audit file.
- The row shows the patrons' names, sorted and separated by ", " (`person-patrons`). It also shows the backing (`person-backing`): the patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, and 0.00 when there are no patrons.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V22__person_patron.sql`, adds a `person_patron` table. The database also rejects duplicates and a person being their own patron.
- **Server:** two new endpoints, written as OfficeFloor pipelines in a new `patron` package:
  - `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/patrons` lists every patron link on the sheet.
  - `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/patrons` adds one. It locks the person's row before checking for a duplicate.
- **Front end:** `features/patrons/` adds the row cell. Backing is worked out in the browser, the same way the existing due-total is. It is built from each patron's own due-total, so holds, floors, late charges and statements carry through.

**Behaviour the request didn't specify:**
- **Sorting:** names are sorted by plain string comparison, so it is case-sensitive.
- **Retired patrons:** a retired person can still be picked as a patron and still counts towards backing.
- **No removal:** patrons can only be added, as the request asked.
